arguments.gap: I need literature evidence on how to improve the expressiveness of a 2D real-valued lookup table (LUT) that uses bilinear interpolation on a fixed uniform 16x16 grid with 256 trainable real parameters, mapping (x,y) in [-1,1]^2 to a real scalar. The candidate must keep total trainable real parameters <= 256. I need papers that address: (1) whether non-uniform / adaptive grid node placement improves approximation of functions with local high curvature compared to a fixed uniform grid under a fixed parameter budget; (2) alternative interpolation schemes (e.g., higher-order, hierarchical/multiresolution, tensor-product, piecewise) that increase expressiveness per parameter for 2D scalar functions; (3) how grid node coordinates vs. node values trade off under a fixed parameter count; (4) any theory on approximation rates of bilinear vs. alternative LUT representations. Selection criteria: papers must contain method-level detail (equations, parameter counts, grid/architecture definitions) that I can read from PDF method pages, and must be about function approximation / interpolation / LUT expressiveness rather than unrelated deep learning. Report paper_finding (original conclusion), transfer_idea (how it could apply), and limitations separately for each paper.
arguments.success_criteria: Return a verified research_report.v1 with at least 2 papers whose PDF method pages were actually read, each with: original title and URL, paper_finding (the paper's own conclusion with the method equations), transfer_idea (concrete adaptation to a 2D LUT with <=256 real parameters), and limitations (why the transfer may not hold). Evidence must distinguish paper findings from my inference. Include enough method detail (equations, parameter counts, grid structure) that I can build an implementable candidate.
